ticker_news.headline: DA Davidson initiates Micron at Buy with aggressive $1,000 price target, citing multi-year AI memory demand supercycle
MU stock surged from ~$420 in mid-April to $636 on May 5 — a ~52% run on AI HBM demand surge and Fitch credit upgrade
Melius Research launches MU at Buy with $700 target; says memory upcycle can run through end of the decade
James Foord downgrades MU from Strong Buy to Buy, flagging that memory supply/demand are approaching equilibrium and upside may be limited
TD Cowen raises MU price target to $660 from $550; says next move depends on durability of AI-driven demand, not more earnings upgrades

analyst_consensus.recent_changes: Overwhelmingly bullish: DA Davidson initiated Buy at $1,000 (May 2026), Melius Research Buy at $700, TD Cowen raised to $660. Counterweight: Erste Group downgraded Buy to Hold (April 2, capex/FCF concerns); James Foord downgraded Strong Buy to Buy (May 5, supply equilibrium risk). Consensus among ~30-58 analysts is Strong Buy; average targets range $549-$582 across major aggregators; high target $1,000, low target ~$400.

web_context.competitor_activity: SK Hynix leads HBM market with ~62% share, Micron at 21%, Samsung at 17%. SK Hynix is investing $12.85B (19 trillion won) in a new memory packaging facility to extend its HBM lead. Samsung is scaling production capacity ~50% in 2026. All three (plus AMD, which reported blowout Q1 results on May 6) are racing to supply Nvidia's next-gen Vera Rubin platform with 16-Hi HBM4; Micron is shipping HBM4 samples at 11 Gbps and has stated it expects to sell out 2026 HBM capacity with an ~$8B annualized HBM revenue run-rate.
web_context.earnings_info: Next earnings: Q3 FY2026, expected approximately June 24, 2026 (some sources say July 1). Analyst EPS estimate: $18.97. FY2026 consensus EPS growth projected at ~605% YoY. Most recent report was Q2 FY2026 on March 18, 2026; Q1 FY2026 revenue was $13.6B (+21% QoQ, +57% YoY).
